subject: Pricing makeup request for delayed multimodel support
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@orbitalcloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature delay impact on Q2 launch — pricing relief request

Kim —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. To follow up: our Q2 product launch is now blocked because the multimodel routing capability (critical for our A/B experimentation) won’t be available in your managed offering until mid-May. That slipped from the Feb timeline in the last roadmap update.

We’re seeing meaningful revenue impact (estimated $150k in incremental bookings pushed to Q3) and are having to absorb extra engineering and GTM costs for a temporary workaround. Given the delay, we’d like Redwood to consider a pricing "makeup" — either a credit against March/April invoices or a short-term discount to offset the lost go-to-market impact while you deliver the feature.

Can you share what flexibility you have here? I’ve attached our March usage report so you can size the ask. We’re also open to a contractual amendment that ties the credit to the GA date of multimodel routing.

Appreciate a fast path here — our board is asking for a mitigation plan.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships
Orbital Cloud
attachments: orbital_usage_march.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@orbitalcloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature delay impact on Q2 launch — pricing relief request

Alicia —

Thanks for the clear note and the usage file. Sorry you’re in this position — we know the multimodel capability is a big enabler for your launch. I’ve looped in Marcus and Lauren to start a coordinated response.

Short-term proposal: we can offer a one-time invoice offset ("pricing makeup") that scales to your committed monthly run-rate while the feature is delayed. To make this happen fast I need: 1) a quick confirm of the contract term and committed monthly spend line to apply the offset against, and 2) permission to draft a short amendment that ties the credit to the GA delivery date.

We’ll need internal alignment with Product and Finance. I’ve copied Sales Ops to help size the offset and Marcus to own the commercial communication. I’ll push for an exec approval window — can you hold off on public comms until we share the formal amendment?

I’ll be back with numbers tomorrow.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Orbital Cloud — pricing makeup request (need product & finance input)

Team —

Customer: Orbital Cloud (DEAL-8347).
Ask: One-time pricing offset or short-term discount to compensate for delayed multimodel routing (roadmap slipped; customer lost Q2 launch momentum). See attached usage file from Alicia.

Immediate questions:
- Product (Karthik): what’s the earliest realistic GA date for multimodel routing? Any interim roadmap workarounds (feature flags, config) we can offer to reduce the impact?
- Finance (Marissa): can you run a quick model for a one-time credit capped at X% of committed monthly run-rate vs. a two-invoice amortized offset? We need to know tax and revenue recognition implications — customer prefers an invoice offset.
- Sales Ops (Lauren): if we propose an offset, how should it be documented (amendment vs. credit memo) to keep legal/CS happy?

Customer expectations: they want a mitigation plan this week. I’d like to propose a conditional makeup credit that is only payable if GA misses mid-May. If Product can commit to a hard date, we can avoid a credit.

Connor — requesting a fast-track exec sign-off if Product confirms the date > mid-May. Please advise on approval limits or if you want Finance to prepare a numeric recommendation.

Thanks — Kim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Orbital Cloud — pricing makeup request (need product & finance input)

Kim, Marcus —

Thanks for the flag. Short answer: the multimodel routing work has dependency on a third-party kernel update that we had expected in March but slipped; current internal ETA for GA is 2027-05-20. We can accelerate by ~1 week if we reallocate 2 engineers and accept a small delta in perf testing surface, but that would create downstream risk for other rollouts.

Interim mitigations: we can provide a configured routing shim (runtime-level routing rules) that covers 70–80% of use cases within 2 business days; it isn’t as smooth as the native multimodel implementation but should unblock their Q2 experiments for limited traffic patterns.

Impact sizing (rough): Orbital’s March committed run-rate suggests an equivalent of $220k/month; the expected launch revenue they called out ($150k) is consistent with 15–20% of their run-rate.

My recommendation: offer the interim routing shim immediately and back it with a conditional pricing makeup equal to 15% of their committed monthly run-rate for two months if GA slips past 2027-05-20. That keeps the remedy proportionate and provides an incentive for us to deliver on the date. Finance/Legal sign-off required.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management — Serving Runtime

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Orbital Cloud — pricing makeup request (need product & finance input)

All —

Agree with the approach. Approve a conditional pricing-makeup up to $45,000 total (cap), to be documented as an amendment to the SOW and amortized across the next two invoices as an invoice offset if GA > 2027-05-20. Conditions:
1) Provide the interim routing shim within 2 business days and a migration plan to GA.
2) Customer must sign the amendment acknowledging the conditional nature tied to GA date.
3) Finance to confirm revenue recognition/tax treatment before we execute.

Marissa — can you confirm the mechanics and any tax/revenue implications? Lauren — please draft the amendment template; include the offset amortization language and link to the HubSpot deal. Kim/Marcus — please communicate this to Alicia ASAP and get a signed amendment (DocuSign).

Once we have the signed amendment, marketing/customer comms can be held by Sales. Thanks for moving fast on this — keep me posted on any pushback.

Connor O'Brien
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
